title: Phase 4 · Minimum Spanning Trees
outline:
Phase 4 video (Algorithms, ECM3428): 'Minimum Spanning Trees', sub line 'The cheapest way to connect everything'. 11 scenes, 120 s: title (4), the problem (11), many trees one cheapest (11), the cut property (14), Prim (13), Kruskal (14), why both are correct (11), the cost (11), from tree to tour (12), the guarantee (10), recap (9). Story: connect every town with the least cable; the answer is a spanning tree (every town linked, no loops, n - 1 cables); a 5-town network has 21 of them and bigger ones far too many to try; the CUT PROPERTY (the cheapest cable across any cut is always safe, proved by swapping) is the engine; Prim grows one tree, Kruskal merges a forest, and each cable either takes is the cheapest across some cut, so both are correct and find the same tree; Prim's array version costs about V^2, Kruskal about E log V, so sparse networks favour Kruskal and dense ones Prim; and an MST gives a travelling-salesman tour at most twice the best (double the tree, skip repeats). Not covered (lesson 4.8 and the workshop): ties (several MSTs), disconnected graphs, clustering by cutting heavy MST edges; the recap points to Workshop 4.W.

LESSONS the facts come from: a4-intro 4.1 (spanning trees), a4-cut 4.2 (cut property), a4-prim 4.3, a4-kruskal 4.4, a4-mst 4.5 (Prim vs Kruskal on the 5-town graph), a4-proof 4.6 (exchange proof), a4-cost 4.7, a4-edge 4.8, a4-tsp 4.9 (MST to tour), a4-build 4.W; js/content/algo/algo-p4-*.js, algo-p4-x-*.js, algo-workshops-4-03.js; bank js/bank/algo-*.js.

THE EXAMPLE NETWORK (scenes 2-7, lessons 4.2 and 4.5): towns A-E, cables AB 4, AC 3, BC 2, BD 5, CD 6, CE 7, DE 1. Minimum spanning tree = AC 3 + BC 2 + BD 5 + DE 1 = 11. Prim from A adds AC, BC, BD, DE (totals 3, 5, 10, 11). Kruskal sorts DE 1, BC 2, AC 3, AB 4, BD 5, CD 6, CE 7: takes DE, BC, AC, rejects AB (A and B already joined through C), takes BD, then stops at 4 cables (CD and CE are never read). Cuts and their safe cable: {A} -> AC, {B} -> BC, {A,B,C} -> BD, {A,B,C,D} -> DE. Swap proof: tree T = AB BC BD DE costs 12; adding AC makes the loop A-B-C; dropping AB gives AC BC BD DE = 11. The network has 21 spanning trees with totals 11 (1), 12 (2), 13 (3), 14 (2), 15 (2), 16 (2), 17 (2), 18 (2), 19 (2), 20 (1), 21 (1), 22 (1). The 8-town network of lessons 4.3-4.4 has 452 spanning trees; 20 towns with every pair linked have 20^18 = 262,144,000,000,000,000,000,000. Cost: array Prim does (V - 1)^2 steps (V = 1024: 1,046,529), Kruskal E log2 V (E = 2048: 20,480, about 50 times less); for V = 1000 and every pair linked (E = 499,500): Prim 998,001, Kruskal 4,977,909 (Prim about 5 times less). Tour (lesson 4.9, seven towns, straight-line distances): MST W = 75.7 (AB, AC, CD, DE, DF, FG), walk ABACDEDFGFDCA = 2W = 151.4, shortcut tour ABCDEFG(A) = 124.8, best tour ABEGFDC = 97.6 (brute force), so 75.7 <= 97.6 <= 124.8 <= 151.4 and the tour is at most 2 x best = 195.2.

VIDEO-WIDE CONVENTIONS. COLOURS (whole video): green = in the tree / kept / safe (a cable or town that belongs to the minimum spanning tree, its total); red = rejected or wasteful (the cable that would close a loop, the dearer cable swapped out, a loop alarm); orange = candidates under test (the cables that cross a cut, the doubled walk of scenes 9-10); blue = a tree or tour we are looking at but have not accepted (the example tree T, the cable being tested in Kruskal, the shortcut tour); purple = the cut (one side X of it; in scene 10 only, also the best possible tour as a dashed benchmark); grey = neutral (cables and towns not in play, tiles not reached). The same example network (five towns A-E at the same positions, the same cable weights) appears in scenes 2-7 so the viewer follows ONE network from scene to scene; scenes 3 and 6-8 draw it smaller. Town letters are 28 px or more, weight pills are 28 px (they do not shrink: keep them off graphs smaller than scale 0.68). Green cables are drawn in the tree, grey ones are not in play, dimmed (o 0.3-0.5) ones are out of the story for now. Every cable and tree state comes from the real algorithm logs in videos/a4/common.js (A4.PRIM, A4.KRUSKAL, A4.CUTS, A4.EXCHANGE, A4.TREES, A4.COST, A4.TSP), which assert every number when the page loads and throw a clear Error if one differs from this storyboard. Symbols (ticks, crosses, arrows, the equals sign) are SVG pictograms (L5.tick/cross/arrow, A4.equals), never glyphs. The headline of the title card is 80 px, because 'Minimum Spanning Trees' wraps at the 92 px of VID.titleCard: scene-01-title.js is finished (a copy of the card with a smaller headline) and must not be replaced by VID.titleCard.

title: Connect every town
with no spare cable
caps: Every cable has a cost. Every town must be linked.
Four cables link all five towns: a spanning tree.
A fifth cable makes a loop. A tree has no loops.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: link every town with as little cable as possible. The answer is a spanning tree: every town reachable, no loops, exactly one cable fewer than there are towns. Shown on the example network: a tree T of four cables, then a fifth cable that closes a loop. COLOURS (whole video): green = in the tree / kept / safe (a cable or town that belongs to the minimum spanning tree, its total); red = rejected or wasteful (the cable that would close a loop, the dearer cable swapped out, a loop alarm); orange = candidates under test (the cables that cross a cut, the doubled walk of scenes 9-10); blue = a tree or tour we are looking at but have not accepted (the example tree T, the cable being tested in Kruskal, the shortcut tour); purple = the cut (one side X of it; in scene 10 only, also the best possible tour as a dashed benchmark); grey = neutral (cables and towns not in play, tiles not reached).

LAYOUT (stage px). THE NETWORK (same in scenes 2-7): const g = A4.net(stage, {x: 24, y: 20, s: 1}) puts the towns at A (64,250), B (214,60), C (264,420), D (454,100), E (584,330) with a weight pill on each cable: AB 4, AC 3, BC 2, BD 5, CD 6, CE 7, DE 1 (pills at the cable midpoints: AB (139,155), AC (164,335), BC (239,240), BD (334,80), CD (359,260), CE (424,375), DE (519,215)). The graph fills x 17-631, y 13-459; the right column x 650-920 is free for counters and tiles, and so is y 470-640. Right column (x 650-920): cables = A4.total(stage, {x: 650, y: 30, w: 270, label: 'cables', tone: 'blue'}); towns = A4.total(stage, {x: 650, y: 130, w: 270, label: 'towns', tone: 'grey'}); fewer = A4.tag(stage, {x: 700, y: 232, text: 'one fewer', tone: 'green'}). Verdict badge under the graph: badge = L5.badge(stage, {x: 24, y: 490, w: 340, h: 68, valid: 'spanning tree', invalid: 'a loop'}) and badge('valid' | 'invalid' | 'none', k) each frame. A cross for the loop: const svg = L5.svg(stage); const cross = svg.appendChild(L5.cross(181, 243, 64, 'red', {w: 9})); L5.drawOn(cross, k) (181, 243 is the middle of the triangle ABC).

DATA (assert at build time with A4.same): the tree T = A4.EXCHANGE.T = ['AB','BC','BD','DE'] (cost 12; it is also the starting tree of scene 4). The fifth cable is AC (cost 3): A4.pathIn(T, 'A', 'C') = ['A','B','C'], so AC closes the loop A-B-C (cables AB, BC, AC, A4.EXCHANGE.cycle).

TIMELINE (local seconds). 0.2-0.9 the five towns pop in, 0.1 s apart: towns[x] = {s: E.pop(k), o: min(1, 4k)} with k = V.ramp(t, 0.2 + 0.1 i, 0.7 + 0.1 i). 1.0-2.5 the seven cables draw on in grey, 0.12 s apart: edges[key] = {k: ramp(t, 1.0 + 0.12 i, 1.4 + 0.12 i)} over A4.EDGE_KEYS (the weight pills pop in by themselves as each cable passes its middle). 2.7 the 'towns 5' counter pops (A4.total .set({text: '5', k})), 2.9 the 'cables 0' counter. 3.0-5.8 lay T one cable at a time, cable j (0..3) starting at 3.0 + 0.8 j and drawing for 0.4 s: edges[key] = {tone: 'blue', solid: true, w: 1.3, k, from} with from 'A' for AB, 'B' for BC, 'B' for BD, 'D' for DE; when a cable arrives its far town turns solid blue (A and B at 3.4, C at 4.2, D at 5.0, E at 5.8) and the cables counter reads j + 1 (bump = V.flash(t, end, end + 0.4)). 6.1-6.8 everything is checked: the five towns turn solid green one after another (0.06 s apart, each with a small pop s 1.15), the four cables turn solid green, the cables counter turns green, badge('valid', ramp(t, 6.3, 6.9)). 7.2-7.7 a fifth cable AC draws on from A in red (edges.AC = {tone: 'red', w: 1.3, k, from: 'A'}). 7.7-9.0 loop alarm: AB, BC and AC get tone 'red' with halo 1 (edges stay solid), the cross draws on (L5.drawOn, ramp(t, 7.8, 8.2)), badge('invalid', ramp(t, 7.8, 8.3)), the cables counter reads 5 in red. 9.0-9.8 the spare cable goes: AC shrinks back towards A (k = 1 - ramp(t, 9.0, 9.6), from 'A'), the cross fades, AB and BC return to solid green, the counter returns to 4 in green, badge('valid') again (ramp 9.4-9.9). 9.6-10.2 the 'one fewer' tag pops in (k = ramp(t, 9.6, 10.2)). 10.2-10.8 hold.

END STATE: the green tree AB BC BD DE on all five green towns, counters 'cables 4' and 'towns 5' with the green 'one fewer' tag, the green 'spanning tree' badge. AC is gone, CD and CE stay grey. Scene 3 starts with the same five towns. CAPTIONS: [[0.4,2.8,"Every cable has a cost. Every town must be linked."],[3.0,6.3,"Four cables link all five towns: a spanning tree."],[6.5,10.5,"A fifth cable makes a loop. A tree has no loops."]]

title: Many spanning trees,
one is cheapest
caps: The same five towns have 21 different spanning trees.
Each one has its own total cost.
The cheapest is the minimum spanning tree.
Bigger networks have far too many trees to try them all.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: the same five towns have 21 spanning trees whose totals run from 11 to 22; the cheapest is the minimum spanning tree. Trying every tree is hopeless for bigger networks. A flip-book of all 21 trees drops one dot per tree onto a cost line, then the count explodes. COLOURS (whole video): green = in the tree / kept / safe (a cable or town that belongs to the minimum spanning tree, its total); red = rejected or wasteful (the cable that would close a loop, the dearer cable swapped out, a loop alarm); orange = candidates under test (the cables that cross a cut, the doubled walk of scenes 9-10); blue = a tree or tour we are looking at but have not accepted (the example tree T, the cable being tested in Kruskal, the shortcut tour); purple = the cut (one side X of it; in scene 10 only, also the best possible tour as a dashed benchmark); grey = neutral (cables and towns not in play, tiles not reached).

LAYOUT (stage px). TOP LEFT the network as a small picture: const g = A4.net(stage, {x: 14, y: 24, s: 0.52, pills: false}) (towns A (34.8,143.6), B (112.8,44.8), C (138.8,232), D (237.6,65.6), E (305.2,185), radius 22, no weight pills). Under it the current tree's total: tot = A4.total(stage, {x: 40, y: 262, w: 260, h: 80, label: 'total', tone: 'blue'}). TOP RIGHT a plot card: a sticker V.h('div', {class: 'v-card plain c-grey', style: left 372, top 14, width 552, height 300}); inside it (stage coordinates) a 28 px dim text 'one dot = one tree' at (392, 26); a grey axis line y 226 from x 390 to 906 (4 px, round caps) with a 10 px tick at every cost x(v) = 404 + (v - 11) * 44 for v = 11..22 and 28 px dim labels (V.h with class 'v-text dim', centred on x(v), top y 238) for 11, 14, 17, 20 and 22; a 28 px dim 'total cost' centred at x 646, top 272. One dot per tree = A4.token(stage, {tone: 'blue', size: 30}) centred at (x(total), 207 - 34 * row), x(total) = 404 + (total - 11) * 44 where row counts the dots of equal total shown before it (the highest stack, total 13, has 3). BELOW: a grey tag A4.tag(stage, {x: 372, y: 324, text: 'how many spanning trees?'}) and the ladder, three rows at y = 380, 450, 520: a 28 px dim label at x 0 (top y + 8) '5 towns', '8 towns', '20 towns', and a bar A4.bar(stage, {x: 180, y, w, h: 56, fs: 34, tone, text}) with w = min(744, 110 + 26 * digits of the count), tone 'blue', 'blue', 'red'; a 28 px dim note 'every pair of towns linked' at (180, 584).

DATA (assert): A4.TREES = the 21 spanning trees sorted by total (A4.TREES[i].keys = its four cables, .total); A4.HIST = {11:1, 12:2, 13:3, 14:2, 15:2, 16:2, 17:2, 18:2, 19:2, 20:1, 21:1, 22:1}; A4.FLIP = the order of the flip-book (index into A4.TREES): the tree 'AB BC BD DE' (total 12, the tree of scenes 2 and 4) first, then 'AB BD CD CE' (22), 'AC BD CE DE' (16), 17 more in a fixed shuffled order, and the cheapest 'AC BC BD DE' (11) last. A4.MST.keys = ['AC','BC','BD','DE'] (total 11). Ladder: A4.COUNTS[r].text = '21' (the five-town network), '452' (the 8-town network of lessons 4.3-4.4, counted by brute force), '262,144,000,000,000,000,000,000' (20 towns with every pair linked: 20^18, Cayley's formula).

TIMELINE. 0.2-0.9 the small network (grey) and the plot card pop in (V.place s 0.9 -> 1, fade), the total pill pops. FLIP-BOOK: tree j (j = 0..20, A4.TREES[A4.FLIP[j]]) is current from start_j: for j < 3 start_j = 1.0 + 0.5 j (shown 0.5 s), for j >= 3 start_j = 2.5 + 0.15 (j - 3) (shown 0.15 s, the last ends at 5.2). While tree j is current: g.update({edges: {each of its 4 cables: {tone: 'blue', w: 1.3}}, base: {edge: {o: 0.5}}}), the total pill shows its total (blue), and its dot drops in from 50 px above its place over 0.25 s (E.out), blue. 5.4-6.4 the cheapest: the network shows the minimum spanning tree in green (cables tone 'green', solid pills not needed, w 1.4, halo 1; towns solid green), the total pill turns solid green and reads 11, the 11 dot (at x 404) turns green and pops (s 1.4 with E.pop), the other 20 dots dim to o 0.55, a green solid tag A4.tag 'cheapest' at (380, 76) pops at 5.6 and a green L5.arrow from (404, 122) to (404, 186) draws on (L5.drawOn, 5.7-6.1) pointing at the 11 dot. 6.6 the header tag pops; the three ladder rows pop at 6.7, 7.5 and 8.3 (label fades in, bar grows k = ramp 0.4 s; rows 1 and 2 show their text at once; row 3 types its number out left to right over 8.4-9.4 with V.type(text, k) while its bar grows to full length 8.3-8.9). 9.5-10.0 the red bar does one small shake (V.place(bar.el, {x: 6 sin(...)}) with a fading envelope). 10.0-10.8 hold.

END STATE: green minimum spanning tree and green '11' pill, the dot plot (one green dot at 11, twenty dimmed blue dots), the three ladder bars. The idea 'so we need a rule that builds the cheapest tree directly' leads into scene 4. CAPTIONS: [[0.4,2.9,"The same five towns have 21 different spanning trees."],[3.0,5.3,"Each one has its own total cost."],[5.4,6.9,"The cheapest is the minimum spanning tree."],[7.0,10.6,"Bigger networks have far too many trees to try them all."]]

title: The cheapest bridge
across a cut is safe
caps: Split the towns into two groups: a cut.
A tree must cross it. AC is the cheapest.
Suppose a tree uses the dearer cable AB.
Add AC: a loop. Drop AB and the tree is cheaper.
The cheapest cable across a cut is always safe.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: split the towns into two groups (a cut). A tree must bridge the gap, and the cheapest bridge is always safe, because any tree that uses a dearer bridge can swap it for the cheapest one and only get cheaper. Shown with the cut {A} | {B, C, D, E} and the swap proof on a real tree. COLOURS (whole video): green = in the tree / kept / safe (a cable or town that belongs to the minimum spanning tree, its total); red = rejected or wasteful (the cable that would close a loop, the dearer cable swapped out, a loop alarm); orange = candidates under test (the cables that cross a cut, the doubled walk of scenes 9-10); blue = a tree or tour we are looking at but have not accepted (the example tree T, the cable being tested in Kruskal, the shortcut tour); purple = the cut (one side X of it; in scene 10 only, also the best possible tour as a dashed benchmark); grey = neutral (cables and towns not in play, tiles not reached).

LAYOUT (stage px). THE NETWORK (same in scenes 2-7): const g = A4.net(stage, {x: 24, y: 20, s: 1}) puts the towns at A (64,250), B (214,60), C (264,420), D (454,100), E (584,330) with a weight pill on each cable: AB 4, AC 3, BC 2, BD 5, CD 6, CE 7, DE 1 (pills at the cable midpoints: AB (139,155), AC (164,335), BC (239,240), BD (334,80), CD (359,260), CE (424,375), DE (519,215)). The graph fills x 17-631, y 13-459; the right column x 650-920 is free for counters and tiles, and so is y 470-640. Right column (x 650): total = A4.total(stage, {x: 650, y: 40, w: 270, h: 80, label: 'tree cost', tone: 'blue'}); the crossing cables as tiles tiles = A4.tiles(stage, {x: 650, y: 170, items: ['AC 3', 'AB 4'], w: 270, h: 56, gap: 12, dir: 'col', tone: 'orange'}); a purple solid tag A4.tag(stage, {x: 20, y: 160, text: 'X', tone: 'purple', solid: true}) above-left of town A; later a green tag 'one cheaper' (A4.tag at (650, 128), tone 'green') and a green L5.tick(780, 235, 70). The loop cross is L5.cross(181, 243, 64, 'red', {w: 9}) from an L5.svg(stage).

DATA (assert): A4.CUTS[0] = the cut X = ['A']: A4.CUTS[0].crossing = AC 3 then AB 4 (A4.crossing(['A'])), safe = AC. A4.EXCHANGE = {X: ['A'], e: 'AC', T: ['AB','BC','BD','DE'] (cost 12), cycle: ['AB','BC','AC'], f: 'AB', T2: ['BC','BD','DE','AC'] (cost 11)}: adding AC to T makes the loop A-B-C; its other cable that crosses the cut is AB (4), which is dearer than AC (3), so swapping AB for AC saves 1. The tree-cost counter goes 12 -> 15 (with the extra cable) -> 11.

TIMELINE. 0.2-1.2 the network pops in (towns pop, cables draw grey 0.06 s apart, pills follow). 1.3-2.4 the cut: g.update({blobs: [{set: ['A'], k: ramp(t, 1.3, 2.0)}]}), the purple 'X' tag pops (k ramp 1.4-1.9), towns A tone 'purple'; the two cables that leave the blob switch to orange with solid pills at 1.8 (edges AB, AC = {tone: 'orange', solid: true, w: 1.2, halo: V.flash(t, 1.8, 2.4)}) while the other five cables dim (base edge o 0.4). 2.2-2.8 the two tiles 'AC 3', 'AB 4' pop in (0.15 s apart, orange). 2.6-3.4 hold; the two orange cables pulse once (halo = V.flash(t, 2.8, 3.4)). 3.6-4.8 the lightest: AC turns solid green (pill solid green, halo 1) and its tile turns solid green; AB and its tile dim to o 0.5. 5.0-5.6 AC becomes a dashed green ghost (edges.AC = {tone: 'green', dash: true, o: 0.8}), the blob, X tag, orange tone and tiles fade out. 5.6-6.9 the example tree T drawn in blue, cable by cable, 0.3 s apart (5.6, 5.9, 6.2, 6.5; 0.35 s each): AB (from 'A'), BC (from 'B'), BD (from 'B'), DE (from 'D'), edges = {tone: 'blue', solid: true, w: 1.3}, towns solid blue when reached; the tree-cost pill pops at 6.4 reading 12. 7.0-7.4 hold. 7.4-8.0 AC draws on from A (solid green, w 1.3, k ramp). 8.3-9.7 loop alarm: AB, BC, AC tone 'red' with halo 1, the cross draws on (8.3-8.7), the tree-cost pill reads 15 in red (tone 'red'). 9.8-10.4 the swap: AB turns dashed red (dash true) and fades (o 0.4 s), a small red L5.cross at AB's middle (g.mid('AB')) flashes; BC, AC, BD, DE turn solid green, the towns solid green; the pill counts 15 -> 11 (round(V.lerp(15, 11, ramp(t, 10.0, 10.6)))) and turns solid green with a bump. 10.6 the green 'one cheaper' tag pops. 10.9 the green tick pops. 11.2-13.5 hold.

END STATE: AB gone, green tree AC BC BD DE on green towns (CD and CE grey, dimmed), green pill 11, 'one cheaper' tag and tick. The same tree is what Prim and Kruskal find next. CAPTIONS: [[0.4,3.0,"Split the towns into two groups: a cut."],[3.2,5.4,"A tree must cross it. AC is the cheapest."],[5.6,8.0,"Suppose a tree uses the dearer cable AB."],[8.2,10.6,"Add AC: a loop. Drop AB and the tree is cheaper."],[10.8,13.5,"The cheapest cable across a cut is always safe."]]

title: Prim grows one tree,
cheapest cable first
caps: Start at any town. Look at every cable leaving the tree.
Take the cheapest one. A new town joins.
Repeat. A cable inside the tree is ignored.
Every town is in. The cheapest tree costs 11.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: Prim grows one tree from a start town. Each step looks at every cable that leaves the tree, takes the cheapest one and adds the new town. Run for real from A on the example network. COLOURS (whole video): green = in the tree / kept / safe (a cable or town that belongs to the minimum spanning tree, its total); red = rejected or wasteful (the cable that would close a loop, the dearer cable swapped out, a loop alarm); orange = candidates under test (the cables that cross a cut, the doubled walk of scenes 9-10); blue = a tree or tour we are looking at but have not accepted (the example tree T, the cable being tested in Kruskal, the shortcut tour); purple = the cut (one side X of it; in scene 10 only, also the best possible tour as a dashed benchmark); grey = neutral (cables and towns not in play, tiles not reached).

LAYOUT (stage px). THE NETWORK (same in scenes 2-7): const g = A4.net(stage, {x: 24, y: 20, s: 1}) puts the towns at A (64,250), B (214,60), C (264,420), D (454,100), E (584,330) with a weight pill on each cable: AB 4, AC 3, BC 2, BD 5, CD 6, CE 7, DE 1 (pills at the cable midpoints: AB (139,155), AC (164,335), BC (239,240), BD (334,80), CD (359,260), CE (424,375), DE (519,215)). The graph fills x 17-631, y 13-459; the right column x 650-920 is free for counters and tiles, and so is y 470-640. Right column (x 650): the candidate list cand = A4.tiles(stage, {x: 650, y: 20, items: ['AC 3', 'AB 4', 'BC 2', 'CD 6'] (4 slots; you change each slot's text per step with cand.set(i, {text})), w: 270, h: 56, gap: 10, dir: 'col', fs: 32}) (y 20-274); the running total tot = A4.total(stage, {x: 650, y: 330, w: 270, h: 80, label: 'tree cost', tone: 'green'}); at the end a green solid tag A4.tag(stage, {x: 650, y: 440, text: 'cheapest tree', tone: 'green', solid: true}). Next to the start town a tag A4.tag(stage, {x: 20, y: 150, text: 'start', tone: 'green'}) and, in step 2 (the third) only, a grey tag 'ignored' at (16, 96).

DATA (A4.PRIM = A4.prim('A'); assert A4.PRIM.order = ['AC','BC','BD','DE'], totals 3, 5, 10, 11): steps[k].X = the towns in the tree before step k ([A], [A,C], [A,C,B], [A,C,B,D]); steps[k].cands = the cables with exactly one end in the tree, cheapest first: step 0 AC 3, AB 4; step 1 BC 2, AB 4, CD 6, CE 7; step 2 BD 5, CD 6, CE 7; step 3 DE 1, CE 7; steps[k].pick = the first of them (AC, BC, BD, DE), steps[k].town = the town that joins (C, B, D, E), steps[k].inside = cables with both ends in the tree that are not in it (step 2: AB; step 3: AB, CD), steps[k].total = tree cost after the step (3, 5, 10, 11), steps[k].tree = its cables.

TIMELINE. 0.2-1.2 the network pops in (grey, pills). 1.2-1.6 town A turns solid green with a pop (s 1.2) and the 'start' tag pops; the total pill pops reading 0. Four steps, step k (0..3) starting at s_k = 1.6 + 2.6 k (1.6, 4.2, 6.8, 9.4); u = t - s_k. Every frame of a step shows: the tree cables so far (steps[k-1].tree, none for k = 0) solid green, the towns of steps[k].X solid green, the cables in steps[k].cands orange with solid pills (w 1.2), the cables in steps[k].inside grey at o 0.3, all other cables grey at o 0.6. u 0-0.5: the candidate cables turn orange and the tiles pop in, slot i showing cands[i] ('AC 3' ...; 0.08 s apart); unused slots stay hidden (o 0). u 0.6-1.0: the cheapest tile (slot 0) turns solid orange and the other tiles dim to o 0.5. u 1.0-1.6: the pick turns solid green (halo flash) and the new town turns solid green with a pop; its tile turns solid green; the other candidate cables go back to grey (o 0.6). u 1.6-2.2: the total counts up to steps[k].total (V.lerp from the previous total) and bumps. u 2.2-2.6: the tiles fade out. In step 2 (u 0.2-1.8) the 'ignored' grey tag shows beside AB, which sits dimmed at o 0.3 (both its ends are in the tree). 12.0-12.8 all five towns and the four cables solid green with halo 1; the green 'cheapest tree' tag pops and a green L5.tick(780, 540, 64) draws on. 12.8-13 hold.

END STATE: the green tree AC BC BD DE (the minimum spanning tree), total 11, 'cheapest tree' tag; CD, CE and AB grey. Scene 6 builds the same tree the other way. CAPTIONS: [[0.4,2.6,"Start at any town. Look at every cable leaving the tree."],[2.8,6.0,"Take the cheapest one. A new town joins."],[6.2,9.6,"Repeat. title: Cheapest cable first,
never close a loop

title: Walk round the tree,
skip the repeats
caps: Start with the minimum spanning tree. Its cost is W.
Walk round it. Every cable is used twice: 2W.
Skip towns already visited. Detours become direct legs.
A round trip, no longer than the walk.

IDEA: a round trip through all seven towns is hard to optimise, but the minimum spanning tree gives a cheap start. title: The tour is never worse
than twice the best
caps: Cut one cable from the best tour: a spanning tree is left.

helpers:
FILES: videos/a4/common.js (pure data and algorithms, no DOM), videos/a4/common-2.js (graph drawing: A4.graph, A4.net, A4.tspMap, blobs, positions), videos/a4/common-3.js (A4.tag, A4.tiles, A4.total, A4.bar, A4.token, A4.marker, A4.equals, geometry). Everything hangs off window.VID.a4; scenes start with const V = window.VID, A4 = V.a4, L5 = V.l5 and const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V. videos/algo-4.html loads engine.js, cards.js, l5/common.js, then a4/common.js, common-2.js, common-3.js, then scene-01 ... scene-11, audio/algo-4.js. l6 is not loaded. Every file starts with a long API comment listing every signature, option and return value: READ THEM FIRST, they are the contract. All draw calls are pure: call them every frame from update(t) with everything you want to see; nothing is remembered between frames; no Math.random, Date or timers (A4.rng(seed) is seeded).

A. DATA (common.js, all asserted at load): A4.TOWNS, A4.EDGES [[a, b, w]], A4.EDGE_KEYS, A4.key(a, b) ('AC' never 'CA'), A4.wOf(key), A4.sumOf(keys), A4.groupsOf(keys), A4.pathIn(keys, a, b), A4.crossing(X) -> [{key, w, a, b}] cheapest first, A4.safe(X), A4.CUTS (4 cuts), A4.EXCHANGE (the swap proof), A4.PRIM (steps with X, cands, pick, town, inside, total, tree), A4.KRUSKAL (sorted, events with accept/path/cycle/before/after/total, unread, cuts), A4.MST {keys, total 11}, A4.TREES (21 spanning trees), A4.HIST, A4.FLIP (flip-book order), A4.COUNTS (21 / 452 / 20^18), A4.COST {sparse, dense} with primText / kruskalText, A4.primSteps, A4.kruskalSteps, A4.big, A4.TSP {mst, W, walk, walkLen, legs, tourLen, best, cut, twiceBest, runW, runWalk, runTour}, A4.num(x, d = 1), A4.commas, A4.rng(seed), A4.same / A4.close (build-time asserts).

B. THE GRAPH (common-2.js): A4.netPos({x, y, s}) / A4.tspPos({x, y, s}) town positions; g = A4.graph(parent, {nodes, edges, r, ew, font, pills, fmt, pillAt, blobs, hidden, letters, edgeBase, townBase}); g.update({edges: {AC: 'green' | {tone, k, o, w, dash, from, halo, pill, pillTone, solid, pillO}}, towns: {A: 'green' | {tone, solid, s, o, dx, dy, ring, ringK, ringDash}}, blobs: [{set, tone, k, dash, fill, pad}], base: {edge, town}, o}); g.pt(town), g.mid(key, f), g.len(key), g.keys, g.r, g.el. A4.net(parent, {x, y, s, ...}) = the example network (pills on, r = max(22, 34 s)); A4.tspMap(parent, {x, y, s}) = the seven towns of lesson 4.9 with all 21 cables hidden until listed. A4.blobPath(points, R) / A4.hull(points) for your own SVG. Cable tones: grey (pale line), green, red, orange, blue, purple; a cable's k grows it from its first letter (or from: 'B'); dash: true makes it dashed (k ignored); the weight pill pops in by itself as k passes 0.5 (pill: 0..1 overrides); solid: true gives a solid sticker pill. Towns: tone soft by default (white when grey), solid: true = filled; ring = a coloured ring with ringK pop-in. A blob is a rounded dashed outline round the towns in `set` (a cut side X or a group), behind everything.

C. SMALL PIECES (common-3.js): A4.tag(parent, {x, y, text, tone, solid, h, fs}) -> .set({text, tone, solid, k, x, y, s, o}); A4.tiles(parent, {x, y, items, w, h, gap, dir: 'row' | 'col', fs, tone}) -> .set(i, {tone, solid, ghost, text, x, y, s, o}), .all(fn), .pos(i), .mid(i); A4.total(parent, {x, y, w, h, label, tone}) -> .set({text, tone, solid, bump, k, o}); A4.bar(parent, {x, y, w, h, tone, solid, text, fs}) -> .set({k, tone, solid, text, textOut, o}), .end(k); A4.token(parent, {tone, size}) -> .set({x, y, s, o, tone}); A4.marker(parent, {x, y, tone, name, text, anchor}) -> .set({k, o, tone, name, text, bump}); A4.equals(x, y, size, tone) -> SVG g; A4.along(points, f) -> {x, y, dx, dy, i}; A4.offsetLine(p, q, off); A4.lerpPt(p, q, f).

D. REUSED FROM videos/l5/common.js (V.l5): L5.tone(name), L5.tick(x, y, size, tone, opt), L5.cross(...), L5.arrow(x1, y1, x2, y2, tone, o, {w, head, bow}), L5.drawOn(g, k), L5.svg(parent) (a full-stage SVG), L5.badge(parent, {x, y, w, h, valid, invalid}) -> badge('valid' | 'invalid' | 'none', k), L5.dice. Do NOT use L5.tourMap / L5.chromosome (different towns, different look).

E. RULES: no white colours (var(--panel) / var(--bg)); labels >= 28 px; everything >= 12 px inside the 936 x 640 stage; update(t) pure; assert every number in the scene file against the storyboard with A4.same(...) when the scene is built; each file < 500 code lines (split a long scene into helpers in the same file or a second part named scene-NN-<slug>-b.js listed in algo-4.html); run npx prettier --write and npx eslint on every file you touch.
